scope.scopeNotesMd: This report analyzes local changes in the core `Patient` StructureDefinition between FHIR R4 4.0.1 and the R6 6.0.0-ballot4 package. Inherited `Element.ele-1` wording/source changes and `Extension.ext-1` snapshot changes are excluded because they are base/datatype behavior rather than Patient-local changes.

SearchParameters, operations, compartments, examples, profiles, implementation guides, and narrative web pages were not assessed except where local StructureDefinitions and terminology artifacts directly informed Patient findings.
Changes inside referenced datatypes such as HumanName, Address, CodeableConcept, Reference, Attachment, Identifier, ContactPoint, and Period are delegated to those datatype reports.

narrativeReportMd:
# Patient R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
Patient keeps the same resource identity in R6, but there is one local hard R4-to-R6 validation break: `Patient.communication.language` now has a required binding to all BCP-47 language tags. The other material local changes are migration and round-trip risks: `Patient.contact.relationship` was semantically split from functional `Patient.contact.role`, and R6 adds contact `additionalName` and `additionalAddress` fields that base R4 cannot natively represent.

## Scope
I compared the R4 and R6 core Patient StructureDefinitions and local Patient-related terminology artifacts in the supplied packages. I excluded inherited/base-artifact changes visible in the Patient snapshot, including `Resource.language`, DomainResource invariants and `modifierExtension`, Element constraints, and Extension constraints.

## Main migration themes
The main R4-to-R6 issue is stricter terminology validation for patient communication language. The main bidirectional semantic issue is contact modeling: R6 separates personal relationship from functional role. The main R6-to-R4 issue is that R6 can now carry multiple contact names and addresses using new core elements that R4 Patient does not have.

## Highest-impact findings
* `Patient:TERMINOLOGY_BINDING:Patient.communication.language:9c3f2d` is the only hard instance-breaking local finding. R4 text-only or local-code communication languages can become R6-invalid.
* `Patient:SEMANTIC_OR_CONFORMANCE_TEXT:Patient.contact.relationship:64b8aa` is not a simple validation break, but it can change business behavior if emergency/billing/interpreter/contact-role data stays in `relationship` instead of moving to `role`.
* `Patient:ELEMENT_PRESENCE_OR_IDENTITY:Patient.contact.additionalName:1f7e42` and `Patient:ELEMENT_PRESENCE_OR_IDENTITY:Patient.contact.additionalAddress:a827de` are R6-to-R4 round-trip risks.

## Findings requiring human review
The contact relationship/role split needs human review because the R6 package references an external v3 personal-relationship value set that is not packaged locally, and no ConceptMap was supplied for deciding which R4 contact-role codes should move to R6 `role` versus remain in `relationship`.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The new contact name/address fields were intentionally added as sibling overflow fields rather than widening existing 0..1 elements, which is a backward-compatible design for generated R4-era models. The communication-language binding tightening and relationship semantic narrowing could have been introduced less disruptively through profiles, warnings, or staged deprecation, but both appear aimed at improving computability and semantic clarity.

## Follow-up analysis
Base reports for Resource/DomainResource/Element/Extension should own the inherited changes visible in Patient snapshots. Terminology follow-up should expand or map the contact relationship and role value sets before automated migration rules are finalized.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: Patient has one hard local R4-to-R6 validation break (`Patient.communication.language` binding is now required), plus material contact-model migration risks. The top concerns are stricter language coding, separating contact personal relationship from functional role, and preserving R6-only contact extra names/addresses when exchanging with R4. The biggest uncertainty is terminology mapping for the contact relationship split.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should normalize `Patient.communication.language` to BCP-47 codings, explicitly map contact relationship codes into R6 `relationship` versus `role`, and define a preservation strategy for R6 `additionalName` and `additionalAddress` when producing R4. Existing R4 instances are otherwise structurally stable: no local Patient elements were removed, local cardinalities and reference targets are unchanged, and choice type sets did not narrow.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for computable Patient StructureDefinition deltas because both assigned StructureDefinitions and package indexes were present. Confidence is medium for exact terminology migration guidance around contact roles because no terminology expansion, official diff, narrative page, or ConceptMap was available, and the R6 package lacks a local copy of the external v3 personal-relationship value set.

findings.title: Patient.communication.language binding changed from preferred common languages to required all BCP-47 languages

oldState.summary: Required element within Patient.communication, but its terminology binding was only preferred to Common Languages.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R4 used the finite/common starter language value set as a preferred binding and also carried a maxValueSet extension pointing to all-languages. Preferred binding violations are not validation errors for base conformance.

semanticText.definition: The ISO-639-1 alpha 2 code in lower case for the language, optionally followed by a region code.
semanticText.comment: R4 explicitly notes that not all systems actually code the language and therefore uses CodeableConcept instead of code.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, a `Patient.communication` entry had to have a `language`, but the base resource only preferred the common language value set. A text-only `CodeableConcept` or a local coding could still be structurally valid, commonly with a terminology warning rather than a validation failure.

newState.summary: Required element within Patient.communication with a required binding to all BCP-47 language tags.

binding.description: IETF language tag for a human language

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R6 all-languages value set composes all codes from `urn:ietf:bcp:47`; it was not locally expanded because BCP-47 is effectively open-ended/external. The binding strength change is directly visible in the Patient StructureDefinition.

semanticText.definition: The language which may be used to communicate with the individual.
semanticText.comment: R6 still acknowledges that not all systems code the language, but the base binding is now required.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6, validators can require a coding from `urn:ietf:bcp:47`/all-languages for `Patient.communication.language`. The starter/common language value set remains as an additional starter binding, not the conformance value set.

facts.note: R6 keeps the common-languages value set only as a starter binding.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct terminology validation break. R4 instances that relied on the preferred binding flexibility--for example a text-only communication language or a local language code--can become R6-invalid because the binding is now required. Runtime risk is high for validators, ETL pipelines, and generated conformance tests that previously treated language coding issues as warnings.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Communication language is operationally important for patient communication and accessibility. Rejected or dropped language data can affect outreach and patient-facing communications, though the change is primarily a validation/conformance issue.

justification.inferredGoal: Require computable IETF BCP-47 language tags while allowing the common language set to remain as starter guidance.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the base binding preferred or extensible to all-languages, with stronger conformance guidance for BCP-47 coding.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal--standardizing patient communication languages on computable BCP-47 tags--is reasonable and clinically/operationally useful. A less-breaking base design could have retained preferred or extensible binding semantics, especially because both R4 and R6 comments acknowledge free-text language capture. However, that alternative would materially weaken the base-resource guarantee that communication language is coded with a standard tag, so the required binding is probably justified despite the hard validation break for text-only or local-code R4 instances.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would keep `Patient.communication.language` as `CodeableConcept` with a preferred or extensible all-languages/BCP-47 binding, retain common languages as starter guidance, and use profiles or best-practice rules where strict coding is required. This would preserve most R4-valid free-text or locally coded instances, but it is only a partial alternative because the core R6 goal appears to be a base-level coded-language guarantee rather than merely migration guidance.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This preserves text/local-code R4 instances but does not guarantee computable BCP-47 language tags in every base R6 Patient.

evidence.detail: R4 binding strength is preferred and valueSet is http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/languages.
R6 binding strength is required and valueSet is http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/all-languages|6.0.0-ballot4, with languages retained as an additional starter value set.
R6 all-languages includes all codes from urn:ietf:bcp:47.

language.text: Preferred spoken language recorded as local free text

examples.examplesMd: The invalid example isolates the terminology issue; it is not intended to prove that every free-text language value has a deterministic BCP-47 mapping.

findings.narrativeMd: `Patient.communication.language` kept the same path, cardinality, and datatype, but its binding became enforceable. This matters because the element is mandatory whenever `Patient.communication` is present. Existing R4 feeds that captured communication language as text or local codes can pass structural validation in R4 but fail terminology validation in R6.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid Patient can become R6-invalid if a `Patient.communication.language` CodeableConcept has no coding from the required all-languages value set. R6-coded language data remains representable in R4 because R4 can carry the same CodeableConcept and already identified all-languages as a maximum value set, though R4 validators would treat the common-languages binding differently.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Migration should normalize communication-language values to BCP-47 where possible and preserve the original display/text when mapping is uncertain. Test cases should cover text-only values, local coding systems, common language tags such as `en`, regional tags such as `en-US`, and sign-language tags. Unmappable values need manual review or an extension/profile-specific policy rather than silent defaulting.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The stronger binding improves computability, but the same goal could have been introduced less disruptively through profiles, a best-practice invariant, or an extensible binding plus conformance guidance. Because R4 explicitly allowed for systems that record language as free text, the base binding-strength increase is a real compatibility cost.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `Patient.communication.language` was a 1..1 `CodeableConcept` with a preferred binding to common languages; R6 keeps the same path, cardinality, and datatype but makes the binding required to `all-languages` / BCP-47. An R4 instance that records the communication language as text only or with a local code can therefore be R4-valid but fail R6 terminology validation. The computable-language goal is reasonable, but this is a hard base validation break on normative Patient content.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition `Patient.communication.language`: min 1, max 1, `CodeableConcept`, preferred binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/languages`; comment says some systems record language as free text.

R6 StructureDefinition `Patient.communication.language`: same cardinality/type, required binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/all-languages|6.0.0-ballot4` with common languages retained only as a starter binding.
R6 `ValueSet-all-languages` includes `urn:ietf:bcp:47`; R4 common-languages value set is a finite starter/common subset.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Patient is supplied as FMM 5 and normative, so a direct old-valid/new-invalid binding-strength increase needs a strong justification. That stability pressure raises this from ordinary migration work to a Revisit finding.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R6 required terminology binding can reject R4 `CodeableConcept` values that have only text or non-BCP-47/local coding; validator and ETL pipelines that previously treated this as a warning may now fail.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design exists: keep a preferred or extensible binding to BCP-47/all-languages, retain common languages as starter guidance, and put strict BCP-47 enforcement in profiles or best-practice rules. The tradeoff is losing a base-level computable-language guarantee, but given normative Patient stability and R4's explicit free-text allowance, the base design should be revisited.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing impact and alternative judgment: the High hard-break assessment is right and the alternative is only partial, but I give more weight to FMM 5/normative stability than the existing 'probably justified' rationale.

findings.title: Patient.contact.relationship was semantically split from functional contact role

oldState.summary: A single relationship element represented the nature of the relationship/contact role, with an extensible binding to patient-contactrelationship.

binding.description: The nature of the relationship between a patient and a contact person for that patient.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R4 value set composes HL7 v2 table 0131 contact-role codes except `O`. Local inspection found codes such as emergency contact, employer, next-of-kin, insurance company, and unknown.

semanticText.definition: The nature of the relationship between the patient and the contact person.
semanticText.requirements: Used to determine which contact person is the most relevant to approach, depending on circumstances.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 used `Patient.contact.relationship` as the single place to express why the contact was relevant. The value set mixed personal and operational contact roles.

newState.summary: relationship is narrowed to personal relationships and a new Patient.contact.role element carries functional roles.

binding.description: The nature of the personal relationship between the patient and the contact person.

semanticText.definition: The nature of the personal relationship between the patient and the contact person.
semanticText.comment: This property is for personal relationships. Functional relationships would be represented in `Patient.contact.role`.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 separates personal relationships from functional roles. `Patient.contact.relationship` is now personal-only, while `Patient.contact.role` is optional and bound, as preferred, to `relatedperson-relationshiptype`.

facts.oldValue: The nature of the relationship between the patient and the contact person.
facts.newValue: The nature of the personal relationship between the patient and the contact person.
Functional relationships would be represented in Patient.contact.role.

facts.note: New R6 element for functional contact roles.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 `relationship` element keeps the R4 path but narrows its definition. The R6 `role` element has complementary comments and requirements that correspond to the functional-role part of the R4 use case.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The binding strength is weaker, so this is not a base validation break for old `relationship` codings. The risk is semantic and runtime: R4 data that encoded emergency-contact, employer, next-of-kin, or similar functional roles in `relationship` may be interpreted as personal relationship data in R6 unless migrated to `role`. Conversely, R6 systems that populate `role` may lose that distinction when exchanging with R4 systems unless they intentionally collapse or extend the data.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Contact role drives who should be contacted in particular situations. Misclassifying a functional role as a personal relationship can affect emergency contact selection, billing contacts, or consent workflows.

justification.inferredGoal: Separate personal relationships from functional contact roles so systems can reason about each independently.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add `Patient.contact.role` while temporarily retaining broad R4 `relationship` semantics and deprecating functional-role use.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Separating personal relationships from functional contact roles is a reasonable R6 modeling goal because R4 mixed family/social relationships with operational roles such as emergency contact or interpreter. A less-breaking design could have added `role` without immediately narrowing `relationship`, but that would only partially meet the goal: consumers would still need to inspect both elements for the same functional facts, and deprecated broad use of `relationship` could persist indefinitely.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would add optional `Patient.contact.role`, keep `Patient.contact.relationship` broad for a transition period, and include explicit guidance to move functional roles to `role`. This is a real base-design alternative, not just conversion tooling, but it has material interoperability costs: validation cannot distinguish old broad use from new personal-only use, duplicate relationship/role encodings may conflict, and the old mixed representation may never disappear.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This eases migration but leaves duplicate same-resource representations for functional roles and risks indefinite semantic ambiguity.

evidence.detail: R4 definition is broad and binding is extensible to patient-contactrelationship.
R6 definition is narrowed to personal relationship and comment says functional relationships are represented in Patient.contact.role.
R6 adds Patient.contact.role 0..* CodeableConcept for functional role, preferred-bound to relatedperson-relationshiptype.
R4 patient-contactrelationship includes HL7 v2 table 0131 with a filter excluding code O.
R6 relatedperson-relationshiptype explicitly includes selected functional/contact role codes such as WIT, ECON, NOK, GUARD, CAREGIVER, E, O, U, INTPRTER, and power-of-attorney variants.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 example shows the intended separation. Base R4 can only natively collapse both concepts into `contact.relationship` or use extensions, so the separation is not losslessly represented in the R4 core model.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 did not remove `Patient.contact.relationship`; instead it narrowed the meaning of the existing element and added a sibling `Patient.contact.role`. This can surprise implementers because old data remains structurally acceptable, but the R6 semantic guidance says functional roles belong somewhere else. A migration that only validates JSON will miss this change.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with functional-role codes in `relationship` are not necessarily R6-invalid because the R6 binding is preferred. They are still behaviorally different: R6 consumers may look at `role` for emergency, billing, interpreter, or power-of-attorney roles and ignore or underweight those codes if left in `relationship`. R6 instances using both `relationship` and `role` are not cleanly representable in base R4 without collapsing fields or using extensions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Create an explicit mapping from R4 contact relationship codes to R6 `relationship` versus `role`. Codes denoting family/friend/personal relationships should remain in `relationship`; emergency contact, employer, billing, interpreter, guardian, next-of-kin, and similar functional roles should move or copy to `role` where a suitable R6 code exists. Because the supplied package has no ConceptMap for this split, high-value contact workflows should be reviewed manually.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The split is model-cleaning rather than a necessary serialization change. A backward-compatible alternative was available: add `role` and keep `relationship` broad until a later version or profile-driven transition. That alternative would reduce migration ambiguity but continue to permit mixed semantics in the base resource.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The R6 package index did not include the external `http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/v3-PersonalRelationshipRoleType` value set referenced by `Patient.contact.relationship`; terminology conclusions are based on the canonical reference, the R4 packaged v3 value set, and the R6 relatedperson-relationshiptype value set.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `Patient.contact.relationship` was broad enough to cover the contact person's relationship or role. R6 keeps the element but narrows it to personal relationship and adds `Patient.contact.role` for functional roles. Existing R4 data with emergency-contact, billing, interpreter, or similar role codes is not automatically invalidated because the R6 relationship binding is preferred, but business logic that now reads `role` can miss unmigrated role facts left in `relationship`.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition `Patient.contact.relationship`: definition is broad, requirements say it helps determine which contact is relevant depending on circumstances, and binding is extensible to `patient-contactrelationship`.
R6 StructureDefinition `Patient.contact.relationship`: definition and comment narrow it to personal relationships and point functional relationships to `Patient.contact.role`.
R6 StructureDefinition `Patient.contact.role`: new 0..* `CodeableConcept` with requirements matching functional contact selection.
R6 `relatedperson-relationshiptype` includes functional/contact role codes such as `ECON`, `NOK`, `GUARD`, `CAREGIVER`, `INTPRTER`, and billing/power-of-attorney variants.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 5/normative status increases concern for changing the meaning of an existing Patient path. The concern is softened because this is not a structural old-valid/new-invalid break, the new `role` element is additive, and the R6 binding on `relationship` is only preferred.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation: the wire path and type remain, but the expected meaning changes; direct downstream runtime behavior can change if contact-selection logic looks in `role` and ignores functional codes still carried in `relationship`.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could add `Patient.contact.role` while leaving `relationship` broad for a transition period and deprecating functional-role use there. That would ease migration, but it would preserve duplicate representations for the same fact and continue the ambiguity R6 is trying to remove.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing Medium semantic/runtime impact and Partial alternative judgment; the independent review supports the same tradeoff even though the normative status makes the migration guidance important.

findings.title: Patient.contact.additionalName adds native support for extra contact names not representable in base R4

oldState.summary: No Patient.contact.additionalName element; Patient.contact.name was limited to 0..1.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed only a single native `Patient.contact.name` for each contact. Additional contact names required extensions, a separate modeled person/contact resource, or local conventions.

semanticText.definition: Additional names for the contact person.
semanticText.comment: R6 says implementers should inspect both Patient.contact.name and Patient.contact.additionalName and treat them as one combined logical list of names.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the original single `name` element and adds a repeatable overflow element for additional names. The comment explicitly frames this as a backward-compatibility design.

facts.note: The existing element was not widened; extra names use a new sibling element.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not R4-to-R6 breaking because the element is optional and newly added. It is a substantial R6-to-R4 round-trip risk: base R4 has no native slot for a second contact name, and R4 clients or generated models will ignore the new field unless explicitly updated.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Alternate contact names can matter for identification and matching, but losing them is usually less severe than losing the contact itself.

justification.inferredGoal: Support multiple names for a contact without changing the cardinality of the existing R4 element.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: this is optional additive R6 content, not an R4-to-R6 base validation break.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of supporting multiple contact names is reasonable, and the chosen R6 design is explicitly less disruptive than changing `Patient.contact.name` from `0..1` to repeating. No R4-valid Patient instance is invalidated by the optional new element, so the backward-compatible-alternative question does not apply as an R4-to-R6 base-design break.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Extension or RelatedPerson-based preservation is useful for R6-to-R4 conversion, but it is a mitigation/down-conversion strategy rather than a less-breaking base R6 alternative. For the base R6 design, adding `additionalName` preserves the old `name` field and cardinality while making extra names first-class in R6; the remaining cost is that base R4 cannot natively carry those additional names.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The R6 design avoids widening `contact.name` but creates R6-to-R4 preservation work for extra names.

evidence.detail: R4 contact.name is 0..1 and no additionalName element exists.
R6 adds additionalName 0..* HumanName with a backward-compatibility comment.

examples.examplesMd: The R4 migration example uses a placeholder extension URL; a real migration should use an agreed cross-version or implementation-guide extension.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds `Patient.contact.additionalName` instead of changing `Patient.contact.name` to repeat. This avoids breaking generated R4 code for the existing field, but it creates new R6 data that older R4 models cannot round-trip in the core Patient shape.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No R4-valid instance becomes invalid in R6 because the new element is optional. A valid R6 instance with `additionalName` cannot be represented in base R4 Patient without data loss, extension use, or conversion to another resource pattern such as RelatedPerson.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: R6 consumers should treat `name` and `additionalName` as one logical list, as the R6 comment instructs. R6-to-R4 conversions should choose a deterministic primary name for `contact.name` and preserve remaining names in a documented extension or external contact/RelatedPerson model. Tests should include multiple name uses, order preservation, and round-trip back to R6.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 design is explicitly more backward-compatible than widening `Patient.contact.name`, because existing code sees the old field unchanged. The cost is a new field that requires application updates and cannot be natively represented in R4.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds optional `Patient.contact.additionalName` while preserving R4's existing `Patient.contact.name` as 0..1. No R4-valid Patient becomes invalid in R6, and the new element is explicitly an overflow field for extra names. The only compatibility issue is reverse conversion: an R6 contact with multiple names cannot be represented losslessly in the base R4 Patient shape.
keyEvidence: R6 StructureDefinition `Patient.contact.name`: remains 0..1 and points alternate/additional names to `additionalName`.
R6 StructureDefinition `Patient.contact.additionalName`: new 0..* `HumanName` with a backward-compatibility comment telling implementers to treat `name` and `additionalName` as one logical list.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 5/normative status supports preserving the existing `name` element and generated API shape. Because the change is optional and additive, the maturity/status does not create a Revisit-level concern.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: extra R6 contact names have no native base R4 slot; there is no old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 mechanism.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking R6 base design is needed for R4-to-R6 compatibility. Making `Patient.contact.name` repeat would be more disruptive to existing generated models; R4 extensions or RelatedPerson-based preservation are down-conversion mitigations, not less-breaking base R6 alternatives.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing impact and alternative judgment: it correctly identifies no R4-to-R6 hard break and no applicable less-breaking base alternative, but I would treat this additive, reverse-only concern as No problem rather than a material break.

findings.title: Patient.contact.additionalAddress adds native support for extra contact addresses not representable in base R4

oldState.summary: No Patient.contact.additionalAddress element; Patient.contact.address was limited to 0..1.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed only a single native address for each patient contact. Multiple addresses required extensions or a different modeling approach.

semanticText.definition: Additional addresses for the contact person.
semanticText.comment: R6 says implementers should inspect both Patient.contact.address and Patient.contact.additionalAddress and treat them as one combined logical list of addresses.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the original single `address` element and adds a repeatable sibling for additional addresses.

facts.note: The existing element was not widened; extra addresses use a new sibling element.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This optional addition does not invalidate R4 data, but base R4 has no native field for multiple contact addresses. Downstream systems that rely on contact address for mail, visits, or legal correspondence can lose data unless conversions preserve the extra addresses explicitly.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Postal or visit addresses for contacts can affect operational communications, emergency planning, or legal notifications.

justification.inferredGoal: Support multiple addresses for a contact without changing the cardinality of the existing R4 element.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: this is optional additive R6 content, not an R4-to-R6 base validation break.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of supporting multiple contact addresses is reasonable, and the selected design avoids a direct cardinality/code-generation break on the existing `Patient.contact.address` field. Because the new element is optional and preserves all R4-valid instances, this finding is best treated as an R6-to-R4 representability concern rather than a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Using an extension or RelatedPerson can preserve extra addresses when converting to R4, but those are mitigation strategies, not evidence of a less-breaking R6 base design. The base R6 addition keeps the old `address` shape intact while adding a first-class place for additional addresses; the tradeoff is that R4 systems need explicit conversion rules to avoid losing extra address data.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The R6 design avoids widening `contact.address` but creates R6-to-R4 preservation work for extra addresses.

evidence.detail: R4 contact.address is 0..1 and no additionalAddress element exists.
R6 adds additionalAddress 0..* Address with a backward-compatibility comment.

examples.examplesMd: The R4 migration example uses a placeholder extension URL to illustrate the need for a documented preservation mechanism.

findings.narrativeMd: `Patient.contact.additionalAddress` is a new R6-native place for extra contact addresses. It is not an R4-to-R6 validation break, but it is important for conversion and generated clients because R4-era code will not see or preserve the new field.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 data remains valid in R6. R6 data using `additionalAddress` is not base-R4 representable without losing all but one contact address or using an extension/external contact resource.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Treat `address` and `additionalAddress` as a single logical address list in R6. For R6-to-R4, select the best primary address for `contact.address`, preserve additional entries through agreed extensions or RelatedPerson, and test address-use prioritization and lossless round-trips where required.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Adding a sibling field is less disruptive than changing `address` cardinality, but it still requires R6-aware clients and explicit down-conversion rules. The design seems justified for backward compatibility with existing generated models.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds optional `Patient.contact.additionalAddress` while preserving R4's existing `Patient.contact.address` as 0..1. This does not invalidate any R4 Patient when moving forward to R6. It does create real reverse-conversion work: an R6 contact with multiple addresses cannot be losslessly represented in the base R4 Patient contact, and choosing which address to keep can affect mail, visit, or legal-notice workflows.
keyEvidence: R6 StructureDefinition `Patient.contact.address`: remains 0..1 and points alternate/additional addresses to `additionalAddress`.

R6 StructureDefinition `Patient.contact.additionalAddress`: new 0..* `Address` with a backward-compatibility comment telling implementers to treat `address` and `additionalAddress` as one logical list.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 5/normative status favors the chosen additive sibling design because it preserves the existing `address` element and API shape. The same status makes address-loss during reverse conversion worth noting, but not enough to make the R6 design disproportionate.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: additional R6 contact addresses have no native base R4 slot, so down-conversion must pick a primary address or preserve extras out of band; there is no old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 mechanism.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No clearly less-breaking base R6 design exists. Repeating `Patient.contact.address` would make the logical model cleaner but would disrupt existing 0..1 generated APIs; extensions or RelatedPerson are useful R6-to-R4 mitigation strategies rather than less-breaking base R6 designs.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing impact and alternative judgment: the finding is not a forward R4-to-R6 break, the R6-to-R4 loss risk is real, and the backward-compatible alternative is not applicable beyond conversion mitigations.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Patient exists in R6 with the same canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, baseDefinition, derivation, abstract flag, and active status.
No local Patient element was removed. Added local Patient elements are covered as findings: `Patient.contact.role`, `Patient.contact.additionalName`, and `Patient.contact.additionalAddress`.
For local Patient elements present in both versions, no min or max cardinality changed. New elements are optional.
No local existing Patient element changed datatype or choice-type membership. `deceased[x]` remains boolean/dateTime and `multipleBirth[x]` remains boolean/integer.

Reference targets for `Patient.contact.organization`, `Patient.generalPractitioner`, `Patient.managingOrganization`, and `Patient.link.other` did not materially change. `Patient.link.other` already allowed Patient and RelatedPerson in R4 and R6.

The local Patient-specific invariant `pat-1` on `Patient.contact` kept the same expression: `name.exists() or telecom.exists() or address.exists() or organization.exists()`. Source metadata changed but validation behavior did not. Base constraints are out of scope.
No local Patient fixed value, pattern value, or default value was added, removed, or changed.
No local Patient maxLength, minValue, maxValue, or regex-style value limit changes were found.
Local Patient modifier semantics are stable: `active`, `deceased[x]`, and `link` remain modifiers. New local contact elements are not modifiers. Inherited modifierExtension changes are out of scope.
Local Patient summary flags on existing Patient elements are materially stable. The visible `Patient.modifierExtension` summary change is inherited from DomainResource and excluded from this report.
No local Patient slicing changes were found in snapshot or differential comparison.

No existing local Patient element changed wire name, choice suffix set, primitive representation, or reference shape. R6 adds new JSON properties for `contact.role`, `contact.additionalName`, and `contact.additionalAddress`, which are addressed in findings.
R6-to-R4 risks are concentrated in the new Patient contact fields and the relationship/role split. No other local R6-only Patient content was found.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Patient root definition broadened beyond current care
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The root definition changed from demographics for an individual or animal receiving care/services to a subject of potential, past, current, or future health-related care, services, or processes. This broadens and clarifies scope but does not change wire format, cardinality, or validation rules for Patient instances.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Business rules that used the R4 wording to exclude future/potential care subjects should be reviewed, but base FHIR validation is not directly affected.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Patient.link text now consistently mentions RelatedPerson
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 and R6 both allow `Patient.link.other` to reference Patient or RelatedPerson. R6 updates the surrounding short/definition/binding description to say Patient/RelatedPerson more consistently, but the targetProfile set and link-type codes did not change.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Implementers with business rules that assumed links only point to Patient should verify that RelatedPerson was already valid in R4 and remains valid in R6.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Administrative-gender required bindings updated version but kept the same code set
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `Patient.gender` and `Patient.contact.gender` still have required bindings to administrative-gender, and the local R4/R6 CodeSystems both contain the same four codes: male, female, other, unknown. The material change is the value set version label, not the accepted code set.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Generated enum packages should update version metadata, but no code remapping is indicated by the local packages.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Patient.link.type required binding kept the same four codes
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The value set version changed from 4.0.1 to 6.0.0-ballot4, but both local CodeSystems define `replaced-by`, `replaces`, `refer`, and `seealso`. The R6 `seealso` definition better reflects RelatedPerson, matching the already-allowed reference target.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Code generators should refresh display/definition text but should not need enum value changes for link type.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: The Patient snapshot shows an inherited `Patient.language` binding change from preferred `languages` to required `all-languages`; under the scope rule this should be assessed in the Resource/base-artifact report, not as a Patient-local finding.

Patient snapshots include inherited DomainResource changes such as contained-resource invariant expression updates and `modifierExtension` summary behavior. These may affect runtime behavior across resources and should be owned by the DomainResource report.
Safe migration of R4 `Patient.contact.relationship` data requires a terminology mapping that decides which old codes remain personal relationships and which move to functional `Patient.contact.role`.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 Patient diff or ballot change note was used. The analysis is based on local package artifacts.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Use an official generated diff/change log for Patient and reconcile it with this StructureDefinition-based report.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Terminology value sets were inspected by compose definitions and local CodeSystems, but no terminology server expansion was run. This especially affects BCP-47 all-languages and v3 relationship-role value sets.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run expansions against the correct R4/R6 terminology package stack and compare code membership and displays.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The R6 package index does not contain a local file for `http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/v3-PersonalRelationshipRoleType`, even though Patient.contact.relationship references it.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Load the matching terminology.hl7.org package or terminology server artifact for the R6 ballot build.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Narrative Patient specification pages and migration notes were not available as local primary inputs. Some semantic intent may be clearer in prose outside StructureDefinition element definitions.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the R6 ballot Patient page, R4 Patient page, and official change notes.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The R6 input is a ballot build (`6.0.0-ballot4`, notForPublication). Findings may change before a final R6 release.
